company: Prairie Mining Limited (now GreenX Metals Limited, ASX: GRX)
title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: PDMRs
tiers.description: Persons Discharging Managerial Responsibilities: any Director or senior executive of the Company who has regular access to Inside Information and the power to make managerial decisions affecting the future development and business prospects of the Company. Subject to an absolute ban on derivatives/hedging (cl 6.3) and margin lending/secured financing (cl 6.4), Closed Periods, and mandatory prior clearance for any other Dealing.

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: Any employee or consultant of the Company told the Policy applies to them, who is not a PDMR. Not subject to the PDMR-specific derivatives or margin lending bans, but must not Deal while possessing Inside Information and, per clause 9.1, must obtain prior clearance for any Dealing.

tiers.name: PCAs
tiers.description: Persons Closely Associated with a PDMR: spouse/equivalent partner, dependent unmarried child/stepchild under 18, a relative sharing the same household for at least a year, or a legal person/trust/partnership managed by, controlled by, set up for the benefit of, or economically equivalent to, such a person. Sections 5-10 and 13 (including the derivatives and margin lending bans and the clearance regime) apply to PCAs; the PDMR must take appropriate steps to ensure their PCAs do not breach the Policy.

definitions.hedging_definition: financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's Securities (including, but not limited to, hedge arrangements)

windows.start_anchor: 10 Business Days before the expected release of announcements regarding material exploration results, resource/reserve estimates, technical studies, sales/production figures, profit/production forecasts, material borrowings, liquidity/cash flow changes, significant operational changes or litigation, mergers/JVs/acquisitions/restructures/takeovers, major asset purchases or sales, material new products/technology, or capital raisings (other than the PDMR's own participation)
windows.end_anchor: 2 hours after the actual release of the relevant announcement

windows.start_anchor: 5 Business Days before the expected release of a disclosure document, takeover target statement, bidder's statement, or scheme booklet involving the Company's Securities
30 calendar days before publication of the Company's annual, half-year or quarterly financial report

Closed Period also automatically extends to any period when the Company is in possession of Inside Information (Schedule 1, Closed Period (d)). Refusals of clearance are not normally explained and must be kept confidential by the applicant (cl 9.4).

rules.detail: Absolute, unconditional ban at all times on Dealing in any financial product issued or created over or in respect of Company Securities, with no clearance route and no vesting-state carve-out. The only carve-out is an option over unissued capital granted by the Company itself (i.e. the LTI grant), not a bank-written option.

exemption_authority: The Approving Officer may grant a PDMR clearance to sell (not buy) ordinary shares only (not other Company Securities) during a Closed Period in Exceptional Circumstances (severe financial difficulty or other extremely urgent, unforeseen, compelling circumstances external to and outside the PDMR's control), described as unlikely to be granted except in rare cases; this exemption never extends to derivatives, hedge arrangements or margin lending/secured financing, which are banned outright for PDMRs with no exemption route at all.

bespoke_clauses.clause: PDMRs are prohibited at all times from Dealing in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's Securities (including, but not limited to, hedge arrangements). For the avoidance of doubt this paragraph does not apply to an option over unissued capital granted by the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank-written OTC collar is squarely a 'financial product ... in respect of' the Company's Securities and is banned outright for PDMRs at all times, with no vesting-state carve-out and no clearance route; the only carve-out is for options the Company itself grants under its incentive plans.

bespoke_clauses.clause: PDMRs are prohibited at all times from entering into margin lending or similar arrangements in respect to Company Securities they hold or in which they have a Relevant Interest.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A loan secured on the PDMR's collared shares (even fully vested) falls within 'similar arrangements' to margin lending and is banned outright with no clearance path, closing off the funded leg entirely for PDMRs.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Sections 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 13 also apply to PCAs of PDMRs, meaning, for each PDMR, PDMRs must take appropriate steps to ensure that their PCAs do not breach this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a spouse, family trust or controlled company does not escape the derivatives or secured financing bans, since the PDMR is responsible for ensuring the PCA also complies.

bespoke_clauses.clause: details of all contracts (other than contracts to which the Company is a party) to which the PDMR is a party or under which the PDMR is entitled to a benefit, and that confer a right to call for or deliver shares in, debentures of, or interests in a managed investment scheme made available by, the Company
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any option/forward contract referencing Company shares, including a bank collar, would itself need to be disclosed to the Company within 1 business day of entry, change or the PDMR ceasing to hold office, even if the Company were not otherwise consulted.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Approving Officer may give clearance during a Closed Period for a PDMR to sell (but not buy) Company shares (but not other Company Securities) in Exceptional Circumstances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even the narrow hardship/court-order relief is limited to selling ordinary shares; it gives no route to enter, unwind or settle a derivative during a Closed Period.

summary: A funded collar is prohibited for anyone who is a PDMR under this policy, which given the definition (any Director or senior executive with regular access to Inside Information and managerial decision-making power) will capture essentially all realistic bank counterparties. Clause 6.3 bans PDMRs from dealing in any financial product created over or in respect of Company Securities (expressly including hedge arrangements) at all times, with no clearance route and no vesting-state exception, and clause 6.4 separately bans PDMRs from margin lending or similar secured arrangements against their Company Securities, also at all times and with no exemption. Both prohibitions extend to the PDMR's closely associated persons (spouse, dependants, controlled trusts/companies), so the structure cannot be routed around them, and even the narrow hardship/court-order relief is limited to selling ordinary shares, never derivatives. Non-PDMR Employees face a materially lighter regime, where derivatives and secured financing arrangements are merely Dealings requiring ordinary prior written clearance outside Closed Periods and while free of Inside Information, so a funded collar could in principle be structured for a genuinely junior, non-PDMR participant, but not for a director or senior executive. This is the only version of the policy available for review and its age (2016) and dual-listing references warrant confirming it is still current before relying on this analysis.
